transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-05
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Diego (Redwood SE), Dr Sarah Lin (Pegasus Head of AI), Raj Patel (Platform), Amelie Durand (Compliance), Tom Weber (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Pegasus is approaching renewal window and wants to add an EU private deployment for data residency and lower latency to EU customers. Primary asks: capacity uplift (steady state + burst), EU private onboarding timeline, compliance pack (SOC2/ISO/KMS), cost tradeoffs (dedicated vs reserved vs private), and a short benchmark to validate latency at 95th pct. Deciding stakeholders: Sarah (owner), Amelie (compliance), Tom/Raj (platform). Redwood to send pricing and schedule benchmarks.

[00:00] Maya: hey everyones, is this a good time? thanks for joining. we have the agenda up — quick renewal check, region onboarding, and bench plan. can i confirm attendees?
[00:28] Dr Sarah Lin: yes hi, thanks maya. we got a couple goals today — want to make sure we can ramp for Q1 traffic and get the eu private plan scoped.
[01:15] Maya: perfect — brief context from our side, pegged renewals for 12/15 but you mentioned wanting an amendment earlier?
[01:42] Raj: yeah we prefer everything signed before the holiday freeze. timeline is tight, we need the private environment to start staging mid-november if possible.
[02:05] Diego: quick thing on staging — we can mirror a private VPC and provide onboarding docs. curious about expected RPS and average token sizes so we can size the pool and recommend quantization profiles.
[02:40] Tom Weber: right now prod sees around 60 rps avg across gen endpoints with spikes to ~320 rps for batch jobs overnight, token lengths variable 150-400, average in the 220 range. latency target is 150ms p50 and 450ms p95 for our interactive flows.
[03:10] Maya: ok good numbers, that helps. for EU private we usually propose a mix — reserved baseline capacity plus a small burst buffer, that keeps unit cost predictable but gives headroom.
[03:48] Dr Sarah Lin: what's the difference cost-wise versus staying on hosted and adding eu region only? we care about data residency and auditability though.
[04:10] Maya: hosted EU region is fastest time-to-value and cheaper upfront, but it doesn't meet your KMS/HSM control and no private control plane. private unlocks key management, dedicated segregation, and audit logs you can ship to your SIEM.
[04:45] Amelie Durand: for us the key parts are KMS integration (we use Azure KeyVault), audit trail retention for 13 months, and SSO with SAML. SOC2 + ISO artifacts also required.
[05:00] Diego: we support customer-managed KMS via our Private control plane and HSM integrations — we have a connector pattern for AKV but will need your IAM and key rotation policies. we'll include sample terraform snippets.
[05:30] Raj: do you have hard SLA numbers for p95? our SLAs in prod are tight and we cant afford big regressions.
[05:55] Maya: our dedicated SLA covers uptime and latency banding; for Private onboarding we commit to performance parity with dedicated pools but we'll run an on-prem like benchmark to baseline. SE to own perf plan.
[06:20] Diego: i'll run two benchmark passes — interactive (RLHF style prompts) and nightly batch ranking. i'll collect p50/p95/p99 and token cost. plan to use model variant M-7B-quant as a baseline and also test an FP16 variant if you want.
[06:55] Tom: can the benchmark include KV-cache scenarios? we rely heavily on prefix caching to reduce latencies for follow-ups.
[07:20] Diego: yes, KV cache included. small note, sometimes transcription says kv cash, ha. we'll test cold and warmed cache to show impact.
[07:40] Dr Sarah Lin: great — also curious about autoscaling and cold start behavior for the private control plane. we saw a few cold spikes on a different provider.
[08:12] Maya: Private supports configured autoscale policies and warm standby pools; for mid-size workloads we recommend a small baseline with vertical scaling and burst policies to limit cold starts.
[09:00] Amelie: security question — do you offer customer-facing audit logs and how granular are they? we need per-request metadata for compliance.
[09:30] Diego: yes, audit logs include request id, model variant, tokens consumed, and route. retention is configurable; default is 90 days but we can extend to 13 months as an add-on.
[10:05] Raj: billing model — if we go private with reserved baseline plus burst, how are tokens billed? presuming tokens for private still show per-token but discounted under reserved commit?
[10:35] Maya: exactly — private is billed as a platform + infra component: a monthly platform fee for private control plane + reserved GPU capacity cost with per-token accounting for extra usage. We'll send sample cost matrices reflecting commitment tiers.
[11:00] Dr Sarah Lin: ok can you approximate numbers for our current 60 rps baseline? rough estimate ok.
[11:20] Maya: rough calc offhand — with your token lengths we'd land in x GPUs baseline, monthly commit in mid-five-figure range, burst buffer for spikes adds small incremental. I'll send a detailed spreadsheet.
[12:30] Diego: tech detail — model compatibility and kernel selection: for quant models we pick kernels tuned for the arch. slight variance in latency depending on sequence lengths; we'll show breakdown in bench.
[13:10] Tom: network topology — will traffic from our EU VPC traverse public internet at any point? need to ensure no egress to non-EU zones.
[13:40] Diego: no, private control plane keeps data in your VPC peered regionally. there are options for private peering and direct connect; we'll work with your network team to define the route.
[14:10] Amelie: re: legal, can we get a standard DPA with EU data-residency clauses?
[14:32] Maya: yes, legal can prep DPA and Data Residency addendum — will include retention and deletion SLA.
[15:00] Speaker 1: — (inaudible) — question about fallback — if the private pool has outage, is there automatic failover to hosted?
[15:20] Diego: we can configure a fallback policy to a hosted compatible model, but that requires agreement on data handling for fallbacks. Many customers prefer no automatic fallback for private data flows due to residency.
[16:00] Dr Sarah Lin: we would prefer fallback only for non-PHI flows; for PHI we want strict no-failover.
[16:28] Maya: noted — that will go into the runbook and the contract.
[18:00] Maya: quick chase on timeline — you mentioned mid-nov staging. is that still target?
[18:22] Raj: yes, if we get onboarding docs and test creds by next wednesday we can start staging 11/16.
[19:10] Diego: OK i'll prepare a test harness and a runbook. two hour bench window, we prefer early morning EU time to capture typical load pattern.
[20:05] Tom: also need a non-prod dataset that's scrubbed; we'll deliver an anonymized dump and a small traffic replay.
[21:00] Amelie: compliance will review your SOC2 binder — can you provide the most recent report and ISO artifacts?
[21:40] Maya: yes will attach SOC2 and ISO PDFs, and a short security whitepaper on encryption-at-rest and KMS integration.
[22:20] Dr Sarah Lin: pricing questions — if we do a 12-month commit vs 6-month extension what discounts exist?
[22:50] Maya: 12-month commit gives steeper discounts on reserved capacity; 6-month is possible as an amendment but pricing delta is modestly higher. We'll put both options in a proposal.
[24:00] Raj: what about capacity headroom for night batch spikes — do you recommend separate batch nodes or same pool?
[24:30] Diego: depends on latency tolerance — if nightly jobs can run with higher latency, separate batch nodes cheaper. If you need consistent latency, a unified pool with burst policy is simpler. We'll model both.
[26:10] Tom: are there any known performance regressions when enabling HSM-backed KMS?
[26:40] Diego: negligible for token path; KMS calls are async and cached — small overhead on key fetches but no measurable model latency impact after warm-up. We'll include telemetry.
[28:00] Maya: ok let's talk deliverables and owners — what do you need from us to get this moving?
[28:22] Dr Sarah Lin: written pricing, security artifacts, benchmark plan, and a draft amendment to route signoff upstream.
[29:05] Maya: will do. Diego will produce bench plan; i'll handle pricing & legal routing.
[30:00] Diego: technical note — we'll include runbook snippets for autoscale, warm standby, and KV cache warming strategies.
[31:20] Amelie: will you support SAML SP-initiated flows and SCIM for group sync?
[31:55] Diego: yes we support SAML and SCIM on the Private control plane; will share config examples.
[33:00] Raj: can we get a one pager of outage fallback options and what triggers them?
[33:25] Maya: yes, that's part of the runbook deliverable.
[34:40] Dr Sarah Lin: one risk — our legal needs to see the KMS flow end-to-end; can you diagram that?
[35:10] Diego: we'll produce an architecture diagram showing key flows and HSM boundaries.
[36:00] Maya: budgetary approval — any estimates to share now so I can start the paperwork?
[36:30] Maya: rough numbers will be in the cost matrix i'll send; if you're comfortable i'll include two commitment scenarios and optional add-ons for longer log retention.
[37:45] Tom: our devs might want to run a small pilot on hosted eu region in parallel to de-risk before private goes live; is that doable?
[38:05] Maya: absolutely — parallel pilot on hosted EU is straightforward and faster; caveat on compliance differences.
[38:45] Amelie: okay, we can do pilot for feature validation but not for PHI.
[39:20] Diego: for the bench plan, propose dates 11/09-11/11 and then a full longer run 11/16 after staging. what's your preference?
[39:50] Raj: 11/09 works for a smoke bench, aim for 11/16 for the full.
[40:30] Maya: great.
[41:10] Dr Sarah Lin: last question — support model during onboarding? will we have an SE during the window?
[41:30] Maya: yes, Diego will be hands-on for the bench and initial activation. CSM will handoff post-activation for runbook ops.
[42:00] Diego: i'll schedule daily 30m standups during the week of staging to speed things up.
[47:30] Maya: quick recap and next steps — i'll send pricing + legal docs by monday 11/08, diego sends bench plan by 11/09, amelia to list compliance docs by 11/07, raj/tom to provision test dataset by 11/10.
[51:45] Dr Sarah Lin: sounds good, thanks all.
[52:00] Maya: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with artifacts and calendar invites.

Action items (as read out in call):
- Maya: Pricing matrix + proposal (due 2026-11-08)
- Diego: Benchmark plan + runbook snippets (due 2026-11-09)
- Amelie: Compliance docs list (due 2026-11-07)
- Raj/Tom: Anonymized test dataset & VPC creds (due 2026-11-10)

End of transcript.
